target.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys. Inherited object properties such as `constructor` and `prototype` were treated as real profile entries in several create, delete, projection, hot-reload, and gateway patch paths. A valid profile with one of those names could therefore be rejected, omitted, or fail to round-trip.

Live route testing also exposed an adjacent deletion failure: when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` or `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH` placed Browser state outside the OS home/temp roots, deleting a launched profile returned HTTP 500 because the trash helper rejected Browser's own configured state directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Use own-property checks at every Browser profile lookup boundary.
- Preserve valid top-level profile keys while continuing to strip nested prototype-pollution keys from untrusted config patches.
- Keep profile listing and hot reload consistent with persisted config.
- Authorize trash moves only from Browser's owned `<config>/browser` subtree. Existing realpath, symlink-escape, target-identity, and trash-destination checks remain in force; the wider config directory is not authorized.

## User Impact

Profiles named `constructor` or `prototype` can be created, listed, hot-reloaded, patched, and deleted normally. Custom state directories outside the home directory work without granting Browser deletion authority over unrelated config or filesystem paths.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `194d41eab680c1964c70087a60e03df607470878`
- Exact GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29032054298 - passed.
- Sanitized AWS Crabbox: lease `cbx_7b2824bafef4`, run `run_231cff1f9ccb`; public networking, no Tailscale, no instance profile, IMDSv2 IAM endpoint 404, exact head verified, Node 24.15 / pnpm 11.2.2; 180 focused tests passed. Lease released.
- Native `OPENCLAW_TESTBOX=1 scripts/pr prepare-run 101694` - passed at the exact PR head.
- Fresh autoreview at the exact head - clean, confidence 0.91.
- Real Express route proof: create and delete `constructor` through `POST /profiles/create` and `DELETE /profiles/constructor`; persistence round-tripped and `Object.prototype` remained unchanged.
- Real Gateway RPC proof: `config.patch` created and removed the profile while nested `constructor` / `prototype` payload keys remained stripped.
- Custom-state route proof: launched/stopped profile deletion under a configured state directory outside home/temp succeeds; unrelated config subtrees, root config authority, and symlink escapes remain rejected.

Live Dev Gateway + OpenAI agent + Browser proof will be added before merge; it is intentionally not claimed by the current evidence.

### 2026-07-12 follow-up: exact-head local proof

- Exact PR head verified locally: `ca0e4b3eff432c1c77cf5ae1810712c9e7570668`.
- Command: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/profiles-service.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.hot-reload-profiles.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/server-context.list-profiles.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/trash.test.ts src/config/merge-patch.proto-pollution.test.ts src/gateway/server.config-patch.test.ts`.
- Result: passed 3 Vitest shards in 104.64s; 7 focused files passed; 139 tests passed.
- Coverage from the focused files: Browser profile own-entry create/list/hot-reload paths, prototype-like profile keys, trash authorization for Browser-owned state, nested prototype-pollution stripping in config merge patches, and Gateway `config.patch` behavior.
- This is exact-head local controlled proof. No live Dev Gateway, external provider, or browser UI session was exercised in this follow-up.
